name: Seasons
use_when: Use for gentle, everyday play where time is measured in seasons, not fights (cozy, village life, slow fantasy).

spring: the river floods the low meadow: someone's garden is under water
a stranger arrives with seeds nobody has seen before
the old bridge needs mending before the fair, and nobody agrees who should pay
lambs, calves and chicks everywhere: one is born that should not have lived
a letter arrives that was sent years ago
the first warm night: everyone is outside, and someone says too much
summer: the well runs low and the village must share
a travelling show sets up in the square for a week
the longest day: a festival, and a contest nobody wants to lose
a fire on the hill: put out in time, but whose was it?
a child goes missing for an afternoon and comes back with a story
the harvest looks too good: someone is already counting the money
autumn: the harvest needs every hand for three days
a death in the village, and what they left behind
the geese leave early: the old folk say a hard winter
the market town raises its prices, and the village must decide
the apple press breaks in the middle of the pressing
someone who left long ago comes home for good
winter: snow closes the road: the village is on its own for a while
the longest night: lanterns, songs, and one empty chair
a sickness goes round; who will nurse whom
the stores run short and someone has been taking more than their share
the lake freezes hard enough to walk to the island
a guest trapped by the snow stays for a week
